Name: self_anchored_temporal_filtering
Title: Self-Anchored Temporal Filtering: LLM-Free Temporal Window Inference for Long-Memory Retrieval
Short Hypothesis: Inferring a temporal window from the timestamp distribution of initial dense retrieval results (via weighted softmax accumulation over sessions) and promoting in-window items via stable partition will match or exceed GPT-4o-based time-range extraction for temporal queries -- requiring zero additional LLM calls.
Related Work: LongMemEval (2024, 268 citations) is a well-established benchmark for long-term conversational memory. Current approaches use GPT-4o for time-range extraction (expensive, brittle). Zep (79 citations) proposes temporal knowledge graphs. Memory-T1 uses RL-based memory selection. LiCoMemory (8 citations) compresses conversation memory. No prior work infers temporal windows from retrieval score distributions for long-memory filtering.

Experiment Plan.model: Stella V5 1.5B (local, ~3GB) + gemini-2.5-flash (for LLM baseline comparison)
notes: Training-free: Stella V5 for embeddings (~3GB on RTX 5080), SATF is pure NumPy
Gemini API used for the LLM baseline comparison (substituting GPT-4o)
Success: Recall@10 improvement >= 0.05 over dense baseline
Clean experimental design with ablations (confidence gating, hyperparameters)
Practical impact: eliminate per-query LLM calls for temporal filtering
